Lenacapavir is a long-acting antiretroviral drug. It targets the HIV-1 capsid, the protein shell that protects the virus’s genetic material, and disrupts several steps in the virus’s life cycle. (accessdata.fda.gov)
On June 18, 2025, the U.S. FDA approved lenacapavir under the brand name Yeztugo for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV-1 through sex. It’s approved for at-risk adults and adolescents who weigh at least 35 kg (77 lb) and test negative for HIV-1 before starting. After the starting doses, it’s given by injection every six months. (accessdata.fda.gov)
The 2025 approval was for prevention, not treatment. The FDA had already approved lenacapavir as Sunlenca in 2022, in combination with other antiretrovirals, to treat certain adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1. (accessdata.fda.gov)
